definition: A single line of rap lyrics. In music, a bar is a measure of time — rappers use it to mean one line or one unit of their verse.
origin: Musical term adopted by hip-hop. DJs and producers count in bars; rappers write in them.
example_lines: Spit 16 bars and the crowd goes crazy
That bar right there was cold

definition: A verse of 16 bars — the standard length for a rap verse on a song. When someone says 'drop a 16,' they mean rap a full verse.
origin: Standard song structure. Verses in hip-hop are typically 16 bars.
example_lines: I need you to drop a 16 on this beat

definition: The payoff line in a rap — the funny, clever, or devastating line that closes a setup. A great punchline rewards the listener for paying attention.
origin: Comedy term brought into hip-hop. Rakim is widely credited with elevating punchlines to an art form.
example_lines: That punchline was so hard I had to rewind it

definition: A song made specifically to insult and attack another artist — exposing their weaknesses, lies, or past actions. The most serious form of rap beef.
origin: Short for 'disrespect track.' A cornerstone of hip-hop culture since the Roxanne Wars in the 1980s.
example_lines: He dropped a diss track and it was over for shorty

definition: A serious dispute or conflict between rappers, crews, or labels. Can be verbal (through music) or escalate to real confrontation.
origin: Slang for argument or grievance. Became central to hip-hop via East Coast/West Coast rivalry of the 90s.
example_lines: The beef between them two goes way back
That's old beef — dead that

definition: A shot taken at someone without naming them directly — could be a metaphor, a shade, or a reference that only the target and insiders will recognize.
origin: Rap beef tactic. Allows artists to attack without being directly called out, maintaining plausible deniability.
example_lines: That was a subliminal — he didn't say no name but everybody knew

definition: The rhythm, cadence, and timing of how a rapper delivers their words over a beat. A good flow fits the music naturally and feels effortless.
origin: Core element of rap technique. Often what separates good rappers from elite ones.
example_lines: His flow on that track is crazy
She switched her flow three times in one verse

definition: Rhyming multiple syllables instead of just the last word. The most technically demanding form of rap lyricism — used by Big Pun, Eminem, and others at the elite level.
origin: Rakim pioneered this in the late 80s. Big L, Big Pun, and Eminem took it to extremes.
example_lines: His multisyllabic rhyme scheme is unmatched

definition: The chorus — the most memorable, repeated part of a song. The hook is designed to stick in your head and carry the song's main message.
origin: Music production term. In hip-hop, hooks are often sung or semi-sung by the rapper or a featured vocalist.
example_lines: That hook is infectious — it's been stuck in my head all week

definition: The spontaneous-sounding phrases or words a rapper says in the background while the main vocals play — 'yeah,' 'uh,' 'let's go,' etc. Often become a rapper's signature.
origin: From Latin 'ad libitum' meaning at one's pleasure. In hip-hop, ad libs are a signature element — think Gucci's 'Burrr' or Lil Uzi's screams.
example_lines: His ad libs go harder than most rappers' verses

definition: Style, fashion, or the way someone carries themselves aesthetically. High drip = looking extremely good. Can also refer to jewelry.
origin: Atlanta, early 2010s. Popularized by Young Thug and the ATL trap scene.
example_lines: The drip is immaculate
He came through with the drip on a thousand

definition: Style, charisma, confidence — the intangible quality that makes someone cool. Similar to drip but more about personality than clothing.
origin: Atlanta/Southern rap. Popularized by Gucci Mane and Young Dolph.
example_lines: Can't teach the sauce, you either got it or you don't

definition: A thousand dollars. 'Racks' typically means multiple thousands. 'A rack' = $1,000. 'Ten racks' = $10,000.
origin: Originated in the South. 'Rack' from the slang for $1,000 bundles of cash.
example_lines: Spent racks on the fit
She need racks just to talk to me

definition: Same as racks — thousands of dollars. A 'band' is $1,000 because bills are banded together in $1,000 bundles at the bank.
origin: Southern rap, popularized in the 2010s.
example_lines: He's pulling bands like it's nothing

definition: 1. A trap house — a location where drugs are sold. 2. A genre of rap music that originated in Atlanta characterized by hi-hat rolls, 808 drums, and dark subject matter about street life.
origin: Atlanta, Georgia. T.I. popularized the term with 'Trap Muzik' (2003). Gucci Mane and Young Jeezy built the sound.
example_lines: Started from the trap, now I'm on top
That's a certified trap banger

definition: The source — the connect. Someone who provides drugs, exclusive goods, or access to things others can't get. 'The plug' is the supplier.
origin: Street term adopted across hip-hop. 'Plug' as in plugging someone in — connecting them to what they need.
example_lines: I'm the plug, they come to me
He hit the plug for a re-up

definition: Diamond jewelry. Specifically refers to diamonds set in chains, rings, watches, and grills. The 'ice' is the sparkle and shine of the diamonds.
origin: New York, late 90s. Popularized by Raekwon ('Iced Out'), then exploded with the bling era (Birdman, Lil Wayne).
example_lines: The ice on his wrist got the club lit
She dripping in ice from head to toe

definition: VVS stands for 'Very Very Slightly Included' — a diamond clarity grade just below flawless. In rap, VVS = the highest-quality diamonds you can get.
origin: Jewelry industry terminology adopted by hip-hop. 2 Chainz and Migos helped bring it into mainstream use.
example_lines: VVS diamonds, no inclusions
That chain got VVS stones all through it

definition: Audemars Piguet — a Swiss luxury watch brand. In rap, wearing an AP (usually the Royal Oak model) signals extreme wealth and status.
origin: Audemars Piguet was founded in 1875. Became a hip-hop status symbol in the 2010s, heavily referenced by Drake, Future, and Migos.
example_lines: AP on my wrist, it's like a disco ball
She only date you if you got the AP

definition: Rolex — the iconic Swiss luxury watch. A Rolex is the most recognizable luxury watch in hip-hop and has been referenced in rap since the 80s.
origin: Rolex has been in rap since Run-DMC. 'Rollie' as a nickname became widespread in the 2000s-2010s.
example_lines: Rollie on the wrist — tell time twice
She only want a man with a Rollie

definition: Patek Philippe — considered by many the most prestigious watch brand in the world, above Rolex. In rap, saying you wear a Patek signals ultra-luxury status.
origin: Patek Philippe founded 1839. Jay-Z's 'Patek Philippe on my wrist' helped cement it in hip-hop vocabulary.
example_lines: Patek on the wrist, f*** a Rolex

definition: Original Gangster — someone who has been in the game from the beginning, earned their respect, and carries authority. OGs are veterans who command deference.
origin: LA gang culture, early 80s. Ice-T popularized it in rap with 'O.G. Original Gangster' (1991).
example_lines: He's an OG, you better show respect
The OGs don't mess with the new generation

definition: Someone who writes raps for an artist who then performs them as their own — without credit. One of the most serious accusations you can make in hip-hop.
origin: Common in the music industry. In hip-hop, it's considered a major violation because authenticity and 'writing your own rhymes' is a core value.
example_lines: They say he uses a ghostwriter — that finished his credibility
Meek Mill exposed his ghostwriter

definition: A guest verse on someone else's song. Artists 'feature' on tracks for a fee, as a favor, or to build relationships. Also called a 'collab.'
origin: Standard practice across music. In hip-hop features became a major business starting in the 90s.
example_lines: That feature he dropped was better than the main artist's verse

definition: Writing ability — the skill of crafting lyrics. 'Strong pen game' means someone writes exceptional bars. The pen is mightier than the rapper who can't write.
origin: Hip-hop term for writing craft. 'The pen' represents the actual writing of lyrics.
example_lines: His pen game is elite — every line hits different

definition: A circle of rappers who take turns freestyling or spitting verses — usually unplanned, raw, and competitive. Ciphers test your skills without studio production.
origin: From '5 Percenter' Nation of Gods and Earths culture, adopted into hip-hop. BET Hip Hop Awards made ciphers famous to mainstream audiences.
example_lines: He bodied that cipher — nobody could touch him

definition: The Roland TR-808 — a drum machine from 1980 whose bass drum sound became the foundation of hip-hop, trap, and R&B. When you feel that deep, rumbling bass kick, that's the 808.
origin: Roland Corporation, 1980. Afrika Bambaataa used it on 'Planet Rock.' It defines modern trap music.
example_lines: That 808 knocked the whole block
Kanye's 808s & Heartbreak changed music forever

definition: Taking a portion of an existing song — usually a melody, drum pattern, or vocal line — and incorporating it into a new track. Sampling is foundational to hip-hop.
origin: Hip-hop's core production technique since the Bronx block parties. DJ Kool Herc invented looping breakbeats.
example_lines: They sampled James Brown — can't go wrong with that
The whole beat is built around that soul sample

definition: Rapping off the top of your head — improvised, unwritten lyrics delivered in real time. True freestyles are a sign of mental quickness and lyrical skill.
origin: Core hip-hop tradition. In the 80s-90s, freestyle battles in New York parks and radio shows determined reputations.
example_lines: He did a 10-minute freestyle off the dome — no notes

definition: To completely destroy someone in a rap battle, verse, or performance. To 'body' a track means to rap so hard that you kill it. If you got bodied, you lost badly.
origin: Battle rap slang. Metaphor: you 'murdered' the track or your opponent so hard they're a body.
example_lines: Kendrick bodied that verse
He bodied everyone in that cipher

definition: A phrase with two meanings — one obvious, one hidden. The hidden meaning is usually more clever, dark, or explicit. One of the highest-value tools in a rapper's lyrical arsenal.
origin: French term for 'double meaning.' Jay-Z, Lil Wayne, and Kendrick are masters of double entendres.
example_lines: That bar was a double entendre — took me a minute to catch it

definition: Someone who gives information to the police or authorities about criminal activity. The absolute worst thing you can be in street culture. 'Snitching' destroys respect.
origin: Street code term. In hip-hop, the 'no snitching' code is central to authenticity.
example_lines: He got labeled a snitch — career over

definition: Social power, influence, and fame — especially online. Having clout means people pay attention to you, follow you, and care what you say.
origin: Old English word for influence/power. Revived and redefined by social media culture in the 2010s.
example_lines: He's chasing clout instead of real respect
All that clout and can't fill a room

definition: A term associated with Brooklyn rap crew linked to Pop Smoke and the Woo gang. Also used as a general exclamation in NYC drill.
origin: Brooklyn, New York. Popularized by Pop Smoke and his Brooklyn drill crew in 2019-2020.
example_lines: Woo! Brooklyn in the building

definition: To smoothly manipulate or trick someone out of their money or possessions — with style. To finesse is to pull off a con so smoothly it looks like skill.
origin: French word for skill/subtlety. In hip-hop it took on the meaning of a smooth hustle.
example_lines: He finessed his way into VIP
She finessed that whole situation

definition: Exciting, electric, or in an amazing state. A 'lit' party is wild and fun. A 'lit' bar is fire. Describes high energy, positive chaos.
origin: AAVE slang going back decades. Reached mainstream usage around 2015-2016 via social media.
example_lines: The section was lit from start to finish

definition: Greatest Of All Time. The ultimate compliment in hip-hop — declaring someone the undisputed best ever. Biggie, Tupac, Jay-Z, Eminem, Nas, Kendrick all have GOAT claims.
origin: Sports term (especially boxing/Muhammad Ali) adopted by hip-hop. LL Cool J popularized it in rap.
example_lines: He's the GOAT — no debate
The GOAT debate in hip-hop never ends

definition: A live battle event (started on Instagram Live) where two artists play their hits back-to-back, letting fans judge who has the better catalog. Created by Timbaland and Swizz Beatz in 2020.
origin: Created during COVID-19 quarantine in 2020. Became a massive cultural event — Gucci vs. Jeezy drew millions.
example_lines: Their Verzuz was the most-watched one ever

definition: Restocking supply — originally drugs, but used broadly for getting more of anything you need. Can also mean re-signing a deal or renewing a contract.
origin: Drug trade terminology adopted into hip-hop vocabulary.
example_lines: Had to hit the plug for a re-up
Time to re-up the contract

definition: When a song sounds incredible, especially on a good sound system. A track that 'slaps' hits hard and makes people react.
origin: West Coast slang going back to the 90s — about how bass-heavy music feels when it hits.
example_lines: That new joint slaps in the whip
Turn this up — it slaps

definition: Compton rapper (born 1987) widely considered the greatest rapper of his generation. Known for conceptual albums (GKMC, TPAB, DAMN.), technical complexity, and his 2024 feud with Drake. Winner of the Pulitzer Prize for DAMN. (2018).
origin: Compton, CA. Signed to TDE. Rose to prominence with Section.80 (2011). Feuded with Drake in 2024.
example_lines: Kendrick dropped 'Not Like Us' and it was over
They call him K-Dot in Compton

definition: Toronto rapper (born 1986), real name Aubrey Drake Graham. One of the best-selling artists ever. Known for melodic delivery, blending rap and R&B, and controversy — including ghostwriting accusations from Meek Mill (2015) and a 2024 feud with Kendrick Lamar.
origin: Toronto, Canada. First known as Jimmy Brooks on 'Degrassi.' Signed to Young Money. Co-founded OVO Sound.
example_lines: Drake responded but the internet wasn't feeling it
OVO is Drake's label

definition: Compton producer and rapper (born 1965). Co-founder of N.W.A, Death Row Records, and Aftermath Entertainment. Discovered Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Kendrick Lamar, and 50 Cent. One of the most important figures in hip-hop history.
origin: Compton, CA. N.W.A (1986). Death Row (1991). Aftermath (1996). The Chronic (1992) defined West Coast rap.
example_lines: Dre produced half the greatest rap albums ever
Forgot About Dre — still hard

definition: Brooklyn rapper (1972-1997), real name Christopher Wallace. Widely considered the greatest rapper of all time by many. 'Ready to Die' and 'Life After Death' are stone-cold classics. Murdered on March 9, 1997.
origin: Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn. Signed to Bad Boy Records by Puff Daddy. East Coast-West Coast beef with Tupac and Death Row.
example_lines: Biggie Smalls is the illest
They called him the Black Frank White

definition: Baltimore/Los Angeles rapper (1971-1996), real name Tupac Amaru Shakur. 2Pac is one of the most iconic figures in hip-hop history — activist, actor, poet. Signed to Death Row. Murdered September 13, 1996.
origin: Born in New York, raised in Baltimore, based in LA. Death Row era included 'All Eyez on Me' and feud with Biggie.
example_lines: Pac died at 25 and left a legacy bigger than most 80-year careers
Westside!

definition: Not lying — this is the truth. 'Cap' means a lie. 'No cap' means no lie, I'm being completely serious.
origin: AAVE slang. Atlanta origins. 'Cap' as slang for lie goes back decades but 'no cap' exploded around 2017-2018.
example_lines: That was the hardest verse of the year, no cap

definition: A lie. 'That's cap' = that's a lie. When someone is 'capping,' they're being dishonest or exaggerating.
origin: AAVE slang. The opposite of 'no cap.'
example_lines: That's cap — he wasn't even there
Stop capping on the internet

definition: Immediate confrontation — the moment you see someone, there's going to be conflict. 'It's on sight' means no conversation, just action.
origin: Street culture term. Means no need for provocation once you see the person.
example_lines: Since the diss dropped, it's on sight
They beef so hard it's on sight every time they cross paths

definition: Don Julio 1942 — a premium tequila. In rap, ordering or sipping 1942 is a signal of wealth and refined taste. The fancy option at the club.
origin: Don Julio's top-shelf aged tequila. Became a luxury status symbol in hip-hop in the late 2010s.
example_lines: Bottles of 1942 all through the section
She only sip 1942

definition: A fight — or specifically, a one-on-one fight. 'Get a fade' means fight me. Also refers to a type of haircut (short on the sides, longer on top).
origin: Dual meaning. As a fight term, it's Southern/universal street slang. As a haircut, it's a classic barbershop term.
example_lines: He caught a fade behind that
Pull up and get this fade
